paragraphs.text: University Valley, Antarctica
Hobo instrumentation deployed in December 2009
SENSOR DEPLOYMENT OVERVIEW
Shallow Ground Ice Site - S77° 51.946’    E160° 43.720’; elevation: ~1697m
• 4-channel external (3 temperature and 1 Echo sensor)
• Hobo Pro v2 (temperature and RH)
Medium Depth Ground Ice Site - S77° 51.773’    E160° 43.527’; elevation: ~1661m
• 4-channel external (4 temperature sensors)
• Hobo Pro v2 (temperature and RH) in soil
• Hobo Pro v2 (temperature and RH) under rock with salt
Deep Ground Ice Site - S77° 51.584’    E160° 43.019’; elevation: ~1684m
• 4-channel external (4 temperature sensors)
• Hobo Pro v2 (temperature and RH) in soil
• Hobo Pro v2 (temperature and RH) under rock with salt
Loggers
4-Channel External Loggers
Logger is placed in a water-resistant plastic box (tupperwear), covered with rocks. Leads of sensors come out of plastic box.
Hobo Pro v2 Temperature & RH Loggers
Loggers are all set at 1 hour data collection intervals, have long white tube with sensor cord.

Medium Depth Ground Ice Site - S77° 51.773’    E160° 43.527’; elevation: ~1661m
Ground ice ~20 cm depth, located midway down valley.
4 channel external industrial logger:  4 temperature probes
1 temperature probe = “HD” = sensor 2
logger name = UniversityValley_Middle_20cmpermafrost
1 hour data collection interval, serial #2432937

Sensor #1 = 10 cm deep.
Sensor #2 = 9 cm into drilled hole into ground ice in diagonal hole.

For deployment, a pit was dug at the site.  Drilled a hole diagonally into ground ice to insert sensor into ground ice.  Remaining probes inserted horizontally into side of pit, sensor 1 inserted 12 cm deep into side of pit.

Another Hobo Pro v2 (T and RH) placed in soil next to the rock, 15 cm deep into soil.
Depth to permafrost at rock/soil location = 22 cm.

paragraphs.text: Jan 11, 2011 (marinova)
Hobo Redeployment – University Valley Dec 2010
All Hobo stations (shallow, medium, deep ice) were downloaded; all the data looks good.

All batteries were replaced at the shallow ice site with no problems or difficulties. All sensors were relaunched to record every 1 hr, but not to record their battery voltage; this allowed us to keep to same recording inverval, but to have them last for > 2 years.

At the medium ice site, the T/RH sensor under the rock stopped functioning after the battery was changed (showed -94C). This is likely due to a disconnect between the sensor and the circuit board, but this was not discovered at the time. The sensor will likely not record any useful data from that point on. The 4-channel external industrial refused to connect to the computer after the battery was changed. The reason for this is completely unknown. All sensors (that could be connected to) were relaunched with a 1 hr measuring interval and no recording of the battery voltage.

At the deep ice site, the 4-channel external industrial sensors had the same failure mode as that at the medium ice site. All other sensors functioned fine after the battery change. The sensors were relaunched to a 1 hr interval and no battery voltage recording.
